text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. This improves navigation for keyboard users and enhances accessibility for individuals with screen readers, allowing them to bypass repetitive content quickly. The trade-off is that it may take up visual space, but the benefit of streamlined access for users with disabilities outweighs this concern.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users never discovering the hidden skip link. A better alternative is a skip link that appears only when focused, using CSS to hide it visually but keep it keyboard-accessible. Settle the argument by testing with keyboard-only users—if they can’t find it, the design fails.

name: Ramp

Add a visually hidden skip link that only appears when keyboard focus arrives. This keeps the page clean for mouse users while guaranteeing keyboard-only users can bypass repetitive content instantly. The trade-off is a small extra CSS rule, but it eliminates the risk of sighted keyboard users missing a hidden link. Testing with keyboard-only users will confirm it works as intended.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users still won’t notice the skip link—even when it appears on focus—because they’re not scanning for hidden elements. A better alternative is a skip link that’s always visible but styled to be subtle (e.g., small, low-contrast text) so it’s discoverable without clutter. Settle the argument by testing with keyboard-only users—if they can’t find it in under 5 seconds, the design fails.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a **large, high-contrast skip link** that is **always visible** at the top of every page, with reduced motion and keyboard-nav support. Result: Skip link visible by default, meets contrast and discoverability needs. Owner: accessibility-w1.
